title: Broken mounting flange (rendered)

title: Broken chain sprocket (06A21)
story: A real 21-tooth chain sprocket (stamped 06A21, marking visible), snapped along a diameter: the top half with about ten teeth is gone. The bore survives, so the mirror stays pinned while it rebuilds the missing teeth.
label: SYNTHETIC COMPOSITE for the app examples: a user-provided photo of a real part placed on a rendered mat, shot by a simulated phone camera. Not a real photo.

truth.basis: CHOSEN 70.0 mm outside diameter: a 06A chain's 9.525 mm pitch gives a 21-tooth pitch diameter of 63.9 mm and an outside diameter of about 69.7 mm
truth.photographed: 64.6 mm tall: the top half snapped off along a diameter

title: Square engine-style gasket
story: A real square gasket with a round bore and eight passages, intact and placed at an angle. Nothing to rebuild: it's measured as photographed, ready to cut a copy from gasket sheet.
label: SYNTHETIC COMPOSITE: a real photo of a real square gasket with a round bore and eight passages (Gasket01.jpg by Miya.m, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons), cut out and placed on a rendered Re-Forge mat at a stated size, shot by a simulated phone camera. Not a real photo of the mat.

truth.basis: 82.2 mm long side, from the same photo's scale, which is CHOSEN: the round flange gasket beside it on the same sheet at Ø100 mm (the outside diameter of a JIS B 2404 10K 20A full-face gasket); the photo has no ruler
truth.photographed: 89.1 × 81.9 mm box on the mat

title: Crankshaft pulley, rim segment snapped off (rendered, guided)
story: A Ø130 mm crankshaft pulley with a rim segment snapped off, taking one bolt hole and two lightening holes with it. guidance.note: Studio: vertical axis through the bore, S4-S21 cut (a circle needs its axis asserted)

title: Spark plug, ceramic wall broken out (user photo)
story: A real Bosch EVO spark plug (user's photo): the right ceramic wall and hex flat broke out, exposing the inner rod. Guided in the Studio — a vertical axis through the plug centre, the S35–S40 break spans, the thread helix and hook electrode kept as designed asymmetry — the mirror rebuilt the missing wall from the intact left side.

guidance.note: Studio: vertical axis, S35-S40 break, helix/hook kept as designed asymmetry

label: REAL USER PHOTO with a Studio session: a user-provided photo of a Bosch spark plug with its right ceramic wall broken out, ruler-scaled at an assumed 100 mm, rebuilt from the stored guidance (asserted vertical axis, S35-S40 break, helix and hook electrode kept as designed asymmetry). Not a render, not a composite.

truth.basis: the intact plug photo (same Bosch EVO model, different vendor shot, same assumed 100 mm; station width ratios within 6 %)
truth.photographed: right wall broken out over S35–S40; rebuilt 100.03 × 19.82 mm, notch fill 25.4 mm² from the mirrored left, helix and hook kept as photographed

title: Steel car wheel, vents hidden by damage (user photo)
story: A real ALCAR steel car wheel (user's photo): a white blob hides three vents on the right. Guided in the Studio — a vertical axis through the hub bore, the blob marked as damage, the visible vents trusted — the mirror rebuilt the three hidden vents where the intact photo shows them.

guidance.note: Studio: vertical axis through the hub bore, white blob marked as damage

label: REAL USER PHOTO with a Studio session: a user-provided photo of an ALCAR steel wheel with three vents hidden by a white blob, ruler-scaled at an assumed 400 mm, rebuilt from the stored guidance (vertical axis through the hub, blob marked as damage). Not a render, not a composite.

truth.basis: the intact wheel photo (same product-shot series, same assumed 400 mm ruler length)
truth.photographed: white blob hides 3 right vents; rebuilt 400.57 × 389.51 mm against intact 400.56 × 389.62 mm; the 3 inferred vents sit within ~2 mm of the intact photo's

title: Sparco steering wheel, rim notch (user photo)
story: A real Sparco suede steering wheel (user's photo) with a notch cut out of the upper-right rim. Guided in the Studio — a vertical axis through the hub, the S98–S33 notch spans, the 3 cutouts and 6 hub bolts trusted (logo and lettering left out) — the mirror rebuilt the missing rim arc from the intact left side, landing within 1 mm of the same photo before the cut.

guidance.note: Studio: vertical axis through hub, S98-S33 notch, cutouts+bolts trusted

label: REAL USER PHOTO with a Studio session and a digitally-cut notch: a user-provided photo of a Sparco steering wheel, ruler-scaled at an assumed 350 mm, with a notch cut out of the upper-right rim in this copy; rebuilt from the stored guidance (asserted vertical axis, S98-S33 notch, 3 cutouts and 6 bolts trusted). Not a render, not a composite; only the damage is digital.

truth.basis: the same photo before the notch was cut (same pixels, same assumed 350 mm: exact)
truth.photographed: rim notch over S98–S33; rebuilt 347.68 × 345.41 mm against intact 347.68 × 345.41 mm; the 77.5 mm inferred rim arc sits within 1.0 mm (mean 0.67 mm) of the intact twin
